1. Core Clinical Tension: A previously healthy man in his 40s presents with subacute fever, hepatosplenomegaly with multiple low-density visceral lesions, and a large solitary pulmonary mass, initially refractory to empiric antibacterials. The primary diagnostic tension lies in differentiating disseminated systemic fungal infection from metastatic malignancy, systemic lymphoma, or HIV-associated opportunistic disease in an immunocompetent-appearing patient who subsequently proves to have idiopathic CD4 lymphopenia (ICL).
2. Admission Breakpoint: Evaluation concludes following admission vital signs, triage hematology/biochemistry, and thoracic/abdominal CT imaging, immediately prior to percutaneous lung, liver, and spleen puncture biopsies.
3. Differential Distinctions: Disseminated fungal infection by dimorphic endemic fungi produces granulomatous pulmonary and visceral lesions. Histoplasmosis exhibits small narrow-based budding intracellular yeasts without a septum. Cryptococcosis produces pleomorphic encapsulated budding yeasts positive on mucicarmine stain. Talaromycosis classically exhibits distinctive intracellular and extracellular sausage-like oval yeast organisms that divide by fission with a prominent transverse midline septum rather than budding.
case_prompt:
A previously healthy man in his 40s was admitted to the hospital with a 15-day history of persistent fever, headache, generalized fatigue, recurrent vomiting, and poor appetite. Ten days prior to admission, he had received an outpatient course of broad-spectrum antibiotics, but his clinical symptoms failed to improve.

On physical examination upon admission, his body temperature was 38.9°C, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute, heart rate 116 beats per minute, blood pressure 130/82 mmHg, and oxygen saturation 98% while breathing ambient air. Examination revealed mild jaundice of the sclerae and skin, along with marked hepatomegaly and splenomegaly.

Admission laboratory investigations revealed a white blood cell count of 6.87 × 10^9/L with 93% neutrophils. Liver biochemistry demonstrated a total bilirubin of 33.9 µmol/L (direct bilirubin 28.7 µmol/L), alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 132 U/L, and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 227 U/L. Inflammatory markers showed a high-sensitivity C-reactive protein of 110.2 mg/L and an erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 19 mm/h.

A computed tomography (CT) scan revealed an irregular mass in the lateral segment of the right middle lobe of the lung measuring 3.7 × 3.0 × 3.2 cm, along with marked enlargement of the liver and spleen containing multiple low-density lesions.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given the solitary pulmonary mass, hepatosplenomegaly with multiple discrete low-density lesions throughout the liver and spleen, jaundice, and systemic B-symptoms (fevers, anorexia, fatigue), but ruled out by fine-needle puncture biopsies that revealed characteristic yeast structures without malignant cells.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Thorough investigations showed no evidence of HIV infection, autoimmune disease, the use of immunosuppressive drugs, and malignancies.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Autoimmune disease or adult-onset immunodeficiency with anti-interferon-gamma autoantibodies
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered as potential etiologies for opportunistic intracellular fungal dissemination in an adult patient lacking overt immunosuppression, but comprehensive immunologic assays for autoimmune conditions and neutralizing autoantibodies were unrevealing.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Serum anti-interferon-gamma autoantibodies testing was negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Percutaneous lung aspiration revealed distinctive sausage-shaped yeast forms with a transverse midline division (fission), with subsequent mycological cultures from blood, bone marrow, liver, and spleen confirming the diagnosis in the context of newly identified idiopathic CD4 lymphopenia (ICL).
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The lung puncture revealed sausage-like shapes yeast organisms with midline septum (Fig. 1C). Mycological cultures from blood, bone marrow, liver and spleen were positive for TM.

editor_comments: Strict admission breakpoint prior to percutaneous organ punctures and fungal cultures. Zero pathogen names in case prompt. Verbatim quotes validated against text.
